title: Towards Standardizing AI Bias Exploration
venue: AIMMES 2024 Workshop on AI bias: Measurements, Mitigation, Explanation Strategies (co-located with EU Fairness Cluster Conference 2024)
extended_summary:
This paper addresses the problem of how to systematically explore and measure bias in AI systems across many fairness concerns, rather than relying on a small set of ad hoc metrics. The authors argue that existing fairness libraries and measures are narrow in scope, context-dependent, and difficult to extend to new settings, especially when fairness concerns involve multiple sensitive attributes, intersections of groups, ranking/recommendation settings, or individual fairness.

To address this, the paper proposes a mathematical framework that decomposes measures of bias into four building blocks: group/subgroup selection, base measures, comparison mechanisms, and reduction mechanisms. Using this framework, the authors show how many existing fairness metrics can be reconstructed and how new variants can be created by recombining components. They also present FairBench, an open-source Python library that implements the framework and provides reusable interfaces for computing and visualizing fairness reports.

The paper is not an empirical study of people, schools, or teachers; it is a framework and software contribution aimed at AI fairness auditing in general computing environments. The authors emphasize that the framework can support systematic bias exploration, backtracking to raw quantities, multidimensional fairness analysis, and interactive report inspection. They conclude that the approach can standardize fairness measurement and facilitate broader exploration of bias concerns, while leaving further taxonomy expansion and additional building blocks to future work.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a theoretical/methods paper with no empirical study, no comparison group, and no educational intervention evaluation. It is peer-reviewed workshop/technical paper content, but it does not meet criteria for experimental or correlational evidence on the requested topic.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper has no measured effect on trust, calibration, error detection, bias, dependence, or longitudinal use in teacher-facing generative AI. Its contribution is infrastructural and conceptual rather than demonstrated impact on educational practice or outcomes.

interventions.use_case: A fairness auditing and measurement library (FairBench) that standardizes decomposition of bias metrics into reusable building blocks for evaluating AI systems across group, subgroup, intersectional, and individual fairness settings.

finding.finding_summary: The paper proposes a mathematical framework and open-source Python library (FairBench) to standardize and systematize fairness auditing across many bias concerns. However, it is a framework/concept paper and does not report empirical effects on educational or learner outcomes (no n, effect size, or confidence interval reported).
finding.measure: Framework utility / fairness-audit standardization; no empirical educational outcome measure reported
